topic: What beamforming strategies ensure consistent LOS connectivity for A2A links in dynamically changing flight formations?
consensus_response: To ensure consistent Line-of-Sight (LOS) connectivity for Air-to-Air (A2A) links, Coordinated Multi-Point (CoMP) techniques with multiple beams and smaller frequency bandwidth can mitigate frequency selective fading and Rician distributed fading effects. Dynamic beamforming schemes adapt to non-stationary spatial channel properties in Elevated Line-of-Sight Air (ELAA), while exploiting the global time reference provided by GPS for synchronization among network nodes enables scheduling contention-free transmissions, reducing interference and increasing capacity.
reference_context: Aeronautical Ad-Hoc Networking involves A2G, A2A, and A2S communications. The aeronautical channel is characterized by rapidly fluctuating frequency selective fading and Rician distributed fading due to high aircraft velocity. CoMP techniques with multiple beams (n_b = 10) and smaller frequency bandwidth (BW_i_UU = 250 MHz) can mitigate these effects, while dynamic beamforming schemes adapt to non-stationary spatial channel properties in ELAA.
